# T06 — AETHER wind tunnel references
Research: TinyFish search then fetch, 2026-11-01.

## Streamline styling
- Streamlines in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ (Volupe): https://volupe.com/simcenter-star-ccm/streamlines-in-simcenter-star-ccm/. Colour lines by velocity magnitude, control thickness, add direction arrows, and animate tracers even for a steady solution. Cross-sections carry more complete field data than lines alone, which is why the wake scanner is a first-class layer rather than an afterthought.
- What I took: thin (≈1.5 px) lines coloured by speed on black, moving tracer pulses at roughly 1 Hz, and a separate scalar plane for quantitative reading.

## Vortex cores
- Q-criterion for vortex visualization (M4 Engineering): https://www.m4-engineering.com/whats-new/q-criterion-for-vortex-visualization. Positive Q marks rotation-dominated regions; the useful threshold is problem dependent, and low thresholds produce too many structures while high thresholds erase the wake. Colour the isosurface by another scalar.
- What I took: two discrete Q levels (low/high) with a translucent tube-like surface, speed colouring, and an explicit legend note that the level is normalised by (U∞/L)².

## Oil flow
- Flow-vis in F1 (Formula 1, Rob Smedley): https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/testing-explained-rob-smedley-on-flow-vis.7nU2VePGlVrhIGa8wgCoLE. Fluorescent powder in light oil leaves ordered surface streaks; aerodynamicists read separation from where the lines break down.
- What I took: thin light streaks over a darkened body, red separation markers, and a legend entry naming the separation heuristic rather than presenting it as measured paint.

## Visual references
- https://volupe.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/1_streamlines1.jpg.webp: dark scene, rainbow speed colouring, thin lines with clear silhouette against black.
- https://www.m4-engineering.com/static/images/blog/q-criterion-for-vortex-visualization/vortex-visualization-q-criterion.gif: coherent translucent vortex tubes, scalar colouring, no opaque clutter.
- https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/content/dam/fom-website/sutton/2019/Testing/BarcelonaTestOne/DayTwo/1017346209-SUT-20190219-DSC_0760-16x9.webp: ordered surface-following streaks, high contrast against the body.

## Decisions
- Bloom is limited to emissive streamline heads; the pressure skin is tone-mapped but capped below the bloom threshold so the car never glows.
- Legends always print min, mid, max and the field unit; ΔCp is centred on zero and labelled with the mapping method.
- Post-processing is disabled automatically below 45 fps for 2 s rather than reducing geometry, so the data density never changes silently.
